root.label: Brookings analysis of U.S. drug supply chain exposure to China

events.label: Brookings analysis of U.S. drug supply chain exposure to China

slots.name: Chinese API exposure
slots.sentence: Our review suggests that Chinese API is included in perhaps a quarter of drug volume sold in the U.S.

slots.name: Branded Chinese API
slots.sentence: The analysis shows that 3% of branded extended units have Chinese API and 8% of generic extended units for drugs excluding IV fluids, with an additional 6% and 16% respectively, where the country is unclear (see Figure 2).

slots.name: DMF China share
slots.sentence: A recent U.S. Pharmacopeia analysis appropriately characterizes the DMF submission data as showing capability, not actual exposure, when discussing China’s share of DMF filings that rose from 5% in 2000 to 32% in 2024.

slots.name: API facility count
slots.sentence: out of the 1,867 facilities listing API manufacture in their operations description, 46% have neither FDA compliance records suggesting branded drug production nor have they paid GDUFA fees.

slots.name: India generic share
slots.sentence: India’s exposure to China matters greatly because of its high share of generic drugs sold in the U.S., 65% of solid oral dose generics.

slots.name: China-only drug count
slots.sentence: We identify 36 such drugs, almost all through the DMF route.

slots.name: No-exposure molecule count
slots.sentence: This list is significantly longer than the list of drugs FDA identified in 2019 as solely sourced from China: capreomycin, streptomycin, and sulfadiazine.

slots.name: India API import share
slots.sentence: the dollar share of Chinese imports (relative to all imported API) has been hovering around 68% plus or minus 2%.

slots.name: Low exposure estimate
slots.sentence: One estimate shows current U.S. reliance on Chinese-made API as low as 8%, while another suggests 47% exposure because of an indirect impact stemming from India’s apparent reliance on China for API.

slots.name: Indirect exposure estimate
slots.sentence: while another suggests 47% exposure because of an indirect impact stemming from India’s apparent reliance on China for API.

slots.name: Global API control estimate
slots.sentence: Some reports have even claimed that China controls 80-90% of the global supply of API.

slots.name: DMF mismatch share
slots.sentence: We find that close to 20% of DMFs filed between 2013 and 2024 do not have a reasonable match with approved drug substances.

slots.name: Chinese DMF count
slots.sentence: But even with GLP-1 DMFs included, the increasing prominence of Chinese DMFs seen in Figure 3a (27% in 2024) is somewhat lower than the 32% in the recent U.S. Pharmacopeia analysis.

slots.name: Chinese facility count
slots.sentence: Among the 417 registered Chinese API facilities, 53% have neither paid GDUFA fees nor have FDA compliance records suggesting branded drug production.

slots.name: API import ton share
slots.sentence: between 2018 and 2023, the share of imports, measured in tons of API (and therefore giving high weight to low potency APIs including antibiotics), has increased from 58% to 75%.

slots.name: India API needs share
slots.sentence: which in 2019 assessed imports to India from all countries at only 32% of India’s API needs

slots.name: India API requirement
slots.sentence: A more recent 2024 analysis from a credit rating agency affiliated with Moody’s put India’s annual API and bulk drug imports at ~35% of its total API requirement.

slots.name: FDA China-only count
slots.sentence: we identify around 360 molecules that include 31 cancer drugs, 14 essential medicines, and all controlled substances (the latter by law).

slots.name: GLP-1 DMF count
slots.sentence: Part of the gap in 2023 and 2024 is due to 17 Chinese GLP-1 DMFs that were likely filed to market GLP-1s for compounding.

slots.name: executive order date
slots.sentence: President Trump issued an executive order in August 2020 directing the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to create a list of essential medicines and critical inputs, to aid in prioritizing domestic production and reducing dependence on foreign suppliers for those products.

slots.name: China API volume share
slots.sentence: China’s share in API production of U.S.-bound drugs must be understood in the context of specific drug categories: it is high for some and low for others. The current aggregate exposure for complete API across all categories is much less than many reports suggest, likely a quarter of the U.S. drug volume, as measured in units.
